title: Is It a Person or a Computer? Tips for Little Kids and AI
summary:
Young children hear AI helpers like Alexa and Siri at home. They may also see videos made by AI on YouTube. Experts say the years before age 8 are a good time to learn what AI is and what it is not.

Researcher Lauren Girouard said preschoolers can already learn from technology. Scientists are still learning how kids use AI at home.

Jennifer Katzenstein of Johns Hopkins All Children's Hospital said parents can explain, "That's the computer answering." Kids can also ask another adult, so they learn the difference between a person's answer and a computer's answer.

Dr. Jenny Radesky said little kids are "much more magical thinkers." Her son thought Siri was a real woman in California until he was 7. She said parents can remind kids that a machine has never felt sad and has no body.

The group Common Sense Media says children 5 and younger should not have AI toys.
why_it_matters: Knowing the difference between a person and a computer helps kids use AI helpers safely and wisely.

keywords.explanation: AI, or artificial intelligence, is computer technology that can answer questions and make things.
Preschoolers are young kids, usually ages 3 to 5, who have not started kindergarten.
Technology means tools and machines, like phones and computers, that people make to do things.
Magical thinkers are people, often little kids, who believe pretend things can be real.
A researcher is a person who studies something carefully to learn new facts.

background_read: AI helpers like Alexa and Siri are computer programs that listen and answer out loud.
Because they talk in friendly voices, little kids may think a real person is speaking.
Experts say early childhood is an important time for learning how the world works.

WHERE: At home, with AI helpers like Alexa and Siri
WHY: Little kids are magical thinkers and may think AI voices are real people
